headline: Get your last fall greens sown this week — the window closes before mid-October frost.

tasks.title: Last-call fall greens
tasks.detail: Direct-sow quick, cold-hardy crops now: spinach, arugula, radishes, leaf lettuce and mustard. With first frost ~4 weeks out, these still have time to mature, and spinach sown now can overwinter under cover for an early spring cut.

tasks.title: Keep picking, and bring in winter squash
tasks.detail: Harvest tomatoes, peppers, beans and summer squash regularly to keep plants producing. Pick winter squash and pumpkins once the rind is hard enough that a thumbnail won't dent it, leaving a bit of stem attached.

tasks.title: Pinch tomatoes to ripen what's on
tasks.detail: Snip off new flowers and pea-sized fruit that won't ripen before frost. This redirects the plant's energy into finishing the fruit already set.

tasks.title: Late blight & powdery mildew
tasks.detail: Cool, damp nights fuel fungal disease. Watch tomatoes for late blight (brown blotches, white fuzz) and squash/cukes for powdery mildew. Remove affected leaves and trash them — don't compost.

tasks.title: Stage your frost protection
tasks.detail: Have row cover or frost cloth ready now so a surprise early cold snap doesn't catch you off guard. First frost on the Seacoast typically lands mid-October, but it can arrive sooner some years.

tasks.title: Ready beds for October garlic
tasks.detail: Clear and amend a bed with compost now so it's set for planting garlic next month. As beds empty out, sow a cover crop like winter rye or mulch bare soil to protect it over winter.
